depressor anguli oris: Pulls the corner of the mouth down (sad expression).
depressor labii inferioris: Pulls the lower lip downwards and outwards.
depressor septi nasi: Pulls the tip of the nose and the septum downwards.
descending part of iliofemoral ligament: Medial limb of the inverted-Y (Bigelow) ligament; the iliofemoral ligament, the strongest ligament in the body, prevents hyperextension of the hip.
descending part of trapezius muscle: Upper fibres from the occiput and nuchal ligament to the lateral end of the clavicle; elevate and upwardly rotate the scapula. Nerve: accessory nerve (XI).
diaphragm: Dome-shaped main muscle of respiration separating the thoracic and abdominal cavities; when it contracts the dome descends and thoracic volume increases. Supplied by the phrenic nerve (C3–C5). Openings: vena cava (T8), oesophagus (T10), aorta (T12).
diaphragmatic fascia: Fascia covering the abdominal surface of the diaphragm.
digastric fossa: Fossa on the inner lower surface of the mandible; the anterior belly of digastric attaches here.
distal phalanx of fifth finger of foot: Distal bone of the little toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
distal phalanx of fifth finger of hand: Distal bone of the little finger; its tip bears the tuberosity of the distal phalanx, which carries the nail bed.
distal phalanx of first finger of foot: Distal bone of the big toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
distal phalanx of first finger of hand: Distal bone of the thumb; its tip bears the tuberosity of the distal phalanx, which carries the nail bed.
distal phalanx of fourth finger of foot: Distal bone of the 4th toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
distal phalanx of fourth finger of hand: Distal bone of the ring finger; its tip bears the tuberosity of the distal phalanx, which carries the nail bed.
distal phalanx of second finger of foot: Distal bone of the 2nd toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
distal phalanx of second finger of hand: Distal bone of the index finger; its tip bears the tuberosity of the distal phalanx, which carries the nail bed.
distal phalanx of third finger of foot: Distal bone of the 3rd toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
distal phalanx of third finger of hand: Distal bone of the middle finger; its tip bears the tuberosity of the distal phalanx, which carries the nail bed.
distal surface of tooth: Surface of a tooth facing the back of the dental arch.
dorsal calcaneocuboid ligament: Thin ligament on the upper surface of the calcaneocuboid joint.
dorsal carpometacarpal ligaments: Bind the distal carpal row to the metacarpal bases from behind.
dorsal cuboideonavicular ligament: Binds the cuboid and navicular from above.
dorsal cuneocuboid ligament: Binds the lateral cuneiform to the cuboid from above.
dorsal cuneonavicular ligaments: Ligaments binding the navicular to the three cuneiforms from above.
dorsal fascia of hand: Fascia covering the extensor tendons on the back of the hand.
dorsal intercarpal ligaments: Ligaments binding the carpal bones to each other from behind.
dorsal intercuneiform ligaments: Bind the cuneiforms to each other from above.
dorsal interossei muscles of foot: Four muscles that move the toes away from the axis of the 2nd toe.
dorsal interossei muscles of hand: Four two-headed muscles between the metacarpals; they move the fingers away from the axis of the middle finger ('DAB'). Ulnar nerve.
dorsal metacarpal ligaments: Bind the metacarpal bases to each other from behind.
dorsal metatarsal ligaments: Bind the metatarsal bases to each other from above.
dorsal parts of lateral intertransversar: Dorsal parts of lateral lumbar intertransversarii
Posterior fibres of the small muscles between the lumbar transverse processes; they bend the trunk sideways.
dorsal radial tubercle: Lister's tubercle; the EPL tendon turns around it on its way to the thumb.
dorsal radio-ulnar ligament: Ligament holding the distal radio-ulnar joint from behind; part of the TFCC.
dorsal radiocarpal ligament: Ligament running from the radius to the proximal carpal bones at the back.
dorsal scaphotriquetral ligament: Dorsal intercarpal ligament running from the scaphoid to the triquetrum at the back.
dorsal surface of sacrum: Convex posterior surface of the sacrum; the deep back muscles attach to it.
dorsal tarsometatarsal ligaments: Ligaments reinforcing the Lisfranc joint from above.
dorsal ulnocarpal ligament: Ligament running from the ulnar side to the carpal bones at the back.
dorsum sellae: Posterior wall of the sella turcica.
eighth rib: 8th rib: a false (vertebrochondral) rib; its cartilage joins the costal cartilage above.
eleventh rib: 11th rib: a floating rib; its front end is free and ends among the muscles of the abdominal wall.
epicranial aponeurosis: Tough tendinous layer of the scalp joining the frontal and occipital bellies; bleeding can spread in the loose layer beneath it.
erector spinae: Deep back muscle made up of the iliocostalis, longissimus and spinalis columns; it holds the spine erect and extends it. Posterior rami of the spinal nerves.
ethmoid bone: Light bone forming the roof of the nasal cavity and the medial walls of the orbits; the olfactory nerves pass through the holes of the cribriform plate, and its labyrinth contains the ethmoidal cells.
ethmoidal notch: Gap between the orbital plates of the frontal bone; the cribriform plate of the ethmoid fits into it.
extensor carpi radialis brevis: Runs from the lateral epicondyle to the base of the 3rd metacarpal; degeneration of its origin tendon is tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis).
extensor carpi radialis longus: Inserts into the base of the 2nd metacarpal; extends the hand and deviates it radially. Radial nerve.
extensor carpi ulnaris: Inserts into the base of the 5th metacarpal; extends the hand and deviates it ulnarly. Posterior interosseous nerve.
extensor digiti minimi: Thin muscle that extends the little finger; it passes through the 5th extensor compartment.
extensor digitorum: Runs from the lateral epicondyle to the extensor hoods of the 2nd–5th fingers; extends the fingers. Posterior interosseous nerve.
extensor digitorum brevis: The only muscle group on the dorsum of the foot; extends the 2nd–4th toes. Deep fibular nerve.
